newsitem.title: USA: Iraqi father charged in teen marriage controversy.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi father charged in teen marriage controversy.

text.p: An Iraqi immigrant was charged with child abuse after he allowed his two teenage daughters to marry men twice their age, police said on Wednesday.

A spokeswoman for the Lincoln Police Department said the father, Salem Alsaidy, allowed his daughters, aged 14 and 15, to marry Iraqi men aged 24 and 28. Nebraska law prohibits marriage before the age of 16.

The husbands were arraigned on Monday in the Lancaster County Courthouse on charges of sexual assault. Alsaidy was also arraigned after being arrested on charges of child abuse and aiding the consummation of a felony.
Members of Lincoln's Iraqi community said the girls were married under Islamic marriage traditions and that the charges against the three men are a case of cultural misunderstanding.
Lancaster County prosecutors declined to comment on the case.
Deputy Lancaster County Prosecutor Jodi Nelson was quoted in the Omaha World-Herald newspaper on Wednesday as having said, "You live in our state, you live by our rules."
